messages:
zoe: heads up — multiple customers opened p99 latency tickets for embeddings in us-west-2 since ~03:00 UTC. two tickets (1234, 1235). seeing p95/p99 regressions on model-serving routes. looks correlated with driver rollout this morning :warning:

deploy-bot: [alert] grafana: https://grafana.internal/r/abc123 - high p99 on /v1/embeddings (us-west-2) - triggered at 03:06 UTC

ashley: investigating. which host pool? I'm seeing gpu-pool-usw2-6 reporting NVMe utilization spikes + host io wait. attaching quick iostat snapshot in a sec.

matt: we pushed NVIDIA driver 525.60 to that pool at 02:40 UTC as part of the automated rollout. rolling window was small but covers the timing. running fio on an affected node now to reproduce.

lee: pls grab iostat -x, nvme top, and blkstat; also check queue_depth and rq_affinity. want to know if it's io stalls or scheduler latencies.

matt: iostat / nvme output from node gpu-usw2-6-12:

```
Linux 5.15.0-rt
Device            r/s    w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm %util
nvme0n1         12.00  230.00  512.00 20480.00  90.0    6.2     18.5   1.2    19.0   0.5   95.4
nvme1n1          8.00  120.00  256.00 10240.00  85.0    5.8     16.1   0.9    17.8   0.4   89.7
```

nvme-cli shows periodic long completion latencies (tail ~20-40ms) and avgqu-sz spikes. blkio stats show flushes from kubelet checkpointing concurrent with serving traffic.

zoe: customer traces show tokenization/first-batch delays ~200-400ms and full-gen p99s hitting 1.0-1.6s. this matches host-level io stalls causing KV-cache misses and longer startup.

katie: we need an immediate mitigation for affected customers and a short-term rollback plan for the driver. can we route affected traffic to another pool/region or a lighter model-variant?

ashley: doing mitigation now: 1) mark gpu-pool-usw2-6 as drainable in the scheduler, 2) apply routing rule to send embeddings -> fallback-embed-2 pool, 3) increase priority for dedicated capacity customers so they don't see reroute. executing step 1+2. :arrow_forward:

deploy-bot: rollout:service-routing update started for embeddings-route - applying weights: primary=0.0, fallback=1.0

matt: also applying temporary host-level IO control to limit background flush storms while we drain. command executed:

```
echo 256 > /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/nr_requests
cgcreate -g blkio:/emergency-throttle
echo "8:0 1048576" > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/emergency-throttle/blkio.throttle.read_bps_device
systemctl restart kubelet  # to reduce checkpoint bursts (temp)
```

lee: after routing + cgroup throttle, p99 on the affected route dropped from ~1.2s to ~320ms within 8 minutes according to the grafana panel. still monitoring for regressions. :white_check_mark:

zoe: customers on tickets 1234/1235 reported improvement and reduced error rates. I'll update the CS notes and ask for confirmation for the next 30m.

ashley: next steps: we should rollback driver 525.60 to 524.XX on gpu-pool-usw2-6 as a temporary fix and add stricter canary gating on future driver rollouts (IO Q-depth & fio smoke). assigning rollback to matt.

matt: acknowledged. will schedule rollback to 524.89 on the pool and run fio stress + nvme perf regression tests in the maintenance window. will coordinate with eng-sre for canary checks.

katie: product will own customer comms + postmortem. action items: 1) postmortem within 72h, 2) driver rollout policy update (add io smoke tests), 3) run broader fleet audit for background flush patterns. I'll create the postmortem doc.

lee: add extra monitoring: alert if avgqu-sz > 3 for >5m on GPU pools during driver change or if nvme completion tail > 10ms for 95th pct.

zoe: updating tickets now. thanks everyone. summary for CS: mitigation applied (evict + routing + cgroup throttle), p99 returned to baseline, rollback scheduled. will follow up in postmortem. :white_check_mark:

ashley: marking incident as mitigated for customer-facing purposes. we'll keep monitoring for 2h before closing. :hourglass:
